mainTopic: Mixtures of forbidden wine, vinegar and leaven: do we decide 'same kind' (משהו) or 'different kind' (נותן טעם) by taste, as אביי says, or by name, as רבא says?
overview: The גמרא discusses forbidden wine mixing with other foods and asks whether a tiny amount (משהו) forbids or only enough to give flavor (נותן טעם). Everyone agrees that old יין נסך on grapes forbids only by נותן טעם. With new wine, אביי says any amount forbids, because we classify by taste and new wine tastes like grapes (מין במינו). רבא says only נותן טעם, because we classify by name and 'wine' and 'grapes' are different names. The גמרא tests this against the משנה, and אביי answers that the משנה is about old wine. The same dispute comes out reversed with mixed vinegars and mixed leavens: there אביי is lenient and רבא is strict. אביי tries to prove his taste rule from a ברייתא about different spices combining, and רבא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds that all prohibitions combine. Finally, the גמרא brings a case of vinegar and wine falling into each other, and the explanation of אביי's view continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Old wine vs. new wine falling on grapes
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that old יין נסך on grapes forbids only by נותן טעם. With new wine, אביי says במשהו and רבא says בנותן טעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If old wine of יין נסך falls on grapes, everyone agrees the grapes are forbidden only if the wine gives them flavor. If new wine falls on grapes, אביי says any amount forbids them, and רבא says only if it gives flavor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a case where all agree, and then a case where אביי and רבא argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old wine clearly tastes different from grapes, so everyone treats it like a different substance, and it forbids only through flavor. New wine has just been squeezed and still tastes like grapes. That similarity is what causes the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Old wine that has already fermented
New wine that was just squeezed
Gives flavor. The mixture is forbidden only if you can taste the forbidden item.
Any amount at all, even a tiny bit

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic question in the laws of mixtures: what makes two things count as the 'same kind'?

phrases.english: Old wine onto grapes,
phrases.notes: He means יין נסך, wine used for עבודה זרה, that fell onto grapes.

phrases.english: all agree: forbidden only when it imparts flavor.
New wine onto grapes,
Abaye says: any amount forbids,
and Rava says: only when it imparts flavor.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַמְרָא עַתִּיקָא בְּעִנְבֵי, דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Old wine on grapes: נותן טעם according to all. New wine on grapes: אביי says משהו, רבא says נותן טעם.

steps.title: אביי's reason: we follow taste
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that we classify by taste. New wine and grapes taste the same, so this is מין במינו, which forbids in any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says any amount forbids, because we go by taste. The wine and the grapes have one taste, so it is the same kind mixed with the same kind, and the same kind forbids in any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי rules that any amount forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on whether this counts as מין במינו or מין בשאינו מינו. For אביי, what decides 'same kind' is the taste. New wine tastes like grapes, so it is the same kind, and the stricter rule of משהו applies.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both
A substance mixed with the same kind of substance

phrases.english: Abaye says: any amount forbids,
because we follow the taste,
and both this and that are one taste,
so it is a substance with its own kind,
and a substance with its own kind forbids in any amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: בְּמַשֶּׁהוּ, בָּתַר טַעְמָא אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind אביי's position in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same kind is decided by taste. New wine and grapes count as מין במינו and forbid in any amount.

steps.title: רבא's reason: we follow the name
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that we classify by name. 'Wine' and 'grapes' have different names, so this is מין בשאינו מינו, which forbids only by נותן טעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says the grapes are forbidden only if the wine gives flavor, because we go by the name. This one has its own name and that one has its own name, so it is a different kind, and a different kind forbids only by giving flavor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא disagrees and requires נותן טעם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees with אביי that the 'same kind' question decides the case. He disagrees about how to measure 'same kind': by what something is called, not by how it tastes. Since wine is called 'wine' and grapes are called 'grapes,' they are different kinds, and the lighter rule of נותן טעם applies.

keyTerms.meaning: A substance mixed with a different kind of substance

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא agree on both rules: same kind forbids in any amount, and a different kind forbids by flavor. They argue only about how to decide whether new wine and grapes are the 'same kind': by taste or by name.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי says we follow taste, so it is מין במינו and forbids במשהו. רבא says we follow name, so it is מין בשאינו מינו and forbids בנותן טעם.

phrases.english: And Rava says: only when it imparts flavor,
because we follow the name,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי שְׁמָא לְחוּד וְהַאי שְׁמָא לְחוּד,
phrases.english: and this has its own name and that has its own name,
so it is a substance with a different kind,
and a substance with a different kind forbids only when it imparts flavor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, בָּתַר שְׁמָא אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's opposing reasoning, parallel to אביי's in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same kind is decided by name. Wine and grapes count as מין בשאינו מינו and forbid only by נותן טעם.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about wine falling on grapes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about יין נסך falling on grapes. It assumes the case is new wine and suggests the משנה requires נותן טעם, which would go against אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: יין נסך that fell on grapes, and so on. We assume this means new wine on grapes. Doesn't the משנה mean it forbids only by giving flavor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the משנה to challenge אביי and support רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attempt rests on two assumptions. First, the משנה is speaking about new wine. Second, it means the grapes are forbidden only through flavor. If both are true, the משנה follows רבא's 'name' approach and goes against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters our mind, meaning we are assuming for now
Is it not...? Used to suggest a reading
Wine poured as an offering to עבודה זרה

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: יֵין נֶסֶךְ שֶׁנָּפַל עַל גַּבֵּי עֲנָבִים כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: We learned: wine of libation that fell on grapes, etc.
phrases.notes: כו׳ means 'and so on.' The משנה goes on to say that cracked grapes become forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין: חַמְרָא חַדְתָּא בְּעִנְבֵי,
phrases.english: It enters our mind: this is new wine on grapes,
is it not that they are forbidden only when it imparts flavor?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: יֵין נֶסֶךְ שֶׁנָּפַל עַל גַּבֵּי עֲנָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the אביי and רבא dispute against the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that new wine on grapes forbids במשהו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה is about new wine and requires נותן טעם, then the משנה goes by name, as רבא says, and not by taste, as אביי says.

steps.title: No: the משנה means any amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. The משנה can be read as forbidding any amount, which fits אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The משנה means any amount forbids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge by reading the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on reading the משנה as נותן טעם. The גמרא answers that the משנה really means משהו. That reading matches אביי, so the משנה is no longer a problem for him.

keyTerms.meaning: No. This rejects the suggested reading.

phrases.english: No, it means any amount forbids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge raised in step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption that the משנה requires נותן טעם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as משהו, which fits אביי's view.

steps.title: The end of the משנה seems to require imparting flavor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי again. The סיפא of the משנה states a rule built on נותן טעם, which suggests the whole משנה is dealing with נותן טעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the end of the משנה: 'This is the rule: anything that benefits from the forbidden item's flavor is forbidden, and anything that does not benefit from its flavor is permitted.' This shows we are dealing with נותן טעם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 5. It points to the closing rule of the משנה, which talks only about flavor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the גמרא said the משנה could mean 'any amount.' But the סיפא sums up the משנה with a rule about flavor. That suggests the earlier case of wine on grapes also needs נותן טעם, which would go against אביי if the case is new wine.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה
Benefit (here, gaining from the forbidden item's flavor)

phrases.english: But from the fact that the last clause teaches:
This is the rule:
anything that benefits from it imparting flavor is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בַּהֲנָאָתוֹ בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם — מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: anything that does not benefit from it imparting flavor is permitted,
this shows that we are dealing with imparting flavor!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reopens the challenge that step 5 deflected, using a different line of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that new wine on grapes forbids in any amount (and step 5's 'any amount' reading of the משנה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא's summary rule is about נותן טעם, so the רישא's case of wine on grapes must also need נותן טעם.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה is about old wine on grapes
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה is talking about old wine on grapes. Everyone agrees that this case needs נותן טעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would אביי explain it? The משנה is about old wine that fell on grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives אביי's answer to the challenge from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 assumed the משנה meant new wine. אביי says it means old wine instead. Old wine tastes different from grapes, so even אביי agrees it forbids only by נותן טעם. That fits the סיפא.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not disprove אביי: he reads it as old wine on grapes, the case everyone agrees needs נותן טעם (step 1).

phrases.english: And Abaye, how does he explain it?
The Mishnah is about old wine on grapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by redefining the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה was about new wine, so its נותן טעם rule would go against אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about old wine, which everyone agrees forbids only by נותן טעם.

steps.title: Mixed vinegars and leavens: אביי says imparting flavor
steps.stepSummary: The same dispute applies to wine vinegar mixed with beer vinegar, and wheat leaven mixed with barley leaven. אביי follows taste. The tastes differ, so it is מין בשאינו מינו and forbids only by נותן טעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wine vinegar and beer vinegar, wheat leaven and barley leaven: אביי says they forbid by נותן טעם. We go by taste, each one has its own taste, so it is מין בשאינו מינו, and מין בשאינו מינו forbids by נותן טעם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case and applies אביי's rule to it. Here אביי's taste rule makes him lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's principle stays the same: we classify a mixture by taste. Wine vinegar and beer vinegar taste different, and so do wheat leaven and barley leaven. So these count as different kinds, and a small amount does not forbid the mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: Beer, a grain drink (so its vinegar is beer vinegar)
A mixture of different kinds; forbids only by נותן טעם

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume אביי is always the strict one. With wine on grapes, taste made him strict. Here the same taste rule makes him lenient. The principle stays fixed, and the result depends on the case.

phrases.english: Wine vinegar and beer vinegar,
and wheat leaven and barley leaven,
phrases.notes: In each pair, one is permitted and one is forbidden, and they got mixed together.

phrases.english: Abaye says: by imparting flavor,
we follow the taste,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי טַעְמָא לְחוּד וְהַאי טַעְמָא לְחוּד,
phrases.english: and this has its own taste and that has its own taste,
so it is a kind mixed with a different kind,
and a kind with a different kind forbids by imparting flavor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wine-on-grapes discussion and applies אביי's taste principle from step 2 to a new pair of cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אביי, mixed wine/beer vinegar and wheat/barley leaven forbid only by נותן טעם, because their tastes differ.

steps.title: Mixed vinegars and leavens: רבא says any amount
steps.stepSummary: רבא follows the name. Both are called 'vinegar' and both are called 'leaven,' so it is מין במינו and forbids in any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: any amount forbids. We go by the name. Both are called vinegar and both are called leaven, so it is מין במינו, and any מין במינו forbids in any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבא's side of the vinegar and leaven cases. Here רבא's name rule makes him strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's principle stays the same as in step 3: we classify by name. With wine and grapes, the different names made him lenient. Here the shared names 'vinegar' and 'leaven' make it the same kind, so even a tiny amount forbids the mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: A mixture of the same kind; forbids in any amount

steps.whatToRemember: אביי follows taste and רבא follows name. With wine on grapes, אביי is strict and רבא is lenient. With vinegars and leavens it flips: אביי is lenient and רבא is strict.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that each אמורא has a consistent principle, and that a single principle can lead to opposite outcomes in different cases.

phrases.english: And Rava says: in any amount,
we follow the name,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי חַלָּא מִיקְּרֵי וְהַאי חַלָּא מִיקְּרֵי,
phrases.english: and this is called vinegar and that is called vinegar,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי חֲמִירָא מִיקְּרֵי וְהַאי חֲמִירָא מִיקְּרֵי,
phrases.english: and this is called leaven and that is called leaven,
so it is a kind mixed with its own kind,
and any kind with its own kind forbids in any amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: בְּמַשֶּׁהוּ, בָּתַר שְׁמָא אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's opposing view on the same cases introduced in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבא, mixed vinegars and mixed leavens forbid in any amount, because they share the same name.

steps.title: אביי proves from mixed spices that we follow taste
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ברייתא that different spices combine to forbid a dish. חזקיה explains this is because they all sweeten. That only makes sense if taste decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know we follow taste? A ברייתא teaches that forbidden spices with two or three names, whether one kind or three kinds, are forbidden and combine. חזקיה said this is about sweet spices, since they all can sweeten the pot. If we follow taste, it works, because they all have one taste. But if we follow names, each one has its own separate name, so why would they combine?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a proof for his view that we follow taste, not name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says three different kinds of spices join together to make a dish forbidden. חזקיה explains they join because they all sweeten, meaning they share one taste. If names decided, three different names could not join, so the ברייתא seems to support אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (an introduction to a proof)
They combine (join together to reach the forbidden amount)
It works out well (if you say...)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא speaks of several different forbidden spices that fell into a permitted dish. The question is whether their small amounts join together to forbid the dish, even though no single spice would forbid it on its own.

phrases.english: Abaye said: From where do I say it
that we follow the taste?
As it is taught: Spices with two or three names,
phrases.notes: These are spices that are forbidden, and each has a different name.

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵן מִין אֶחָד, אוֹ מִין שְׁלֹשָׁה —
phrases.english: and they are one kind, or three kinds,
are forbidden and combine.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: הָכָא בְּמִינֵי מְתִיקָה עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: And Chizkiya said: Here we are dealing with sweet kinds,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וּרְאוּיִן לְמַתֵּק בָּהֶן אֶת הַקְּדֵירָה.
phrases.english: since they are fit to sweeten the pot with them.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בָּתַר טַעְמָא אָזְלִינַן —
phrases.english: It works well if you say we follow the taste:
they are all one taste,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ בָּתַר שְׁמָא אָזְלִינַן —
phrases.english: but if you say we follow the name,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי שְׁמָא לְחוּד וְהַאי שְׁמָא לְחוּד!
phrases.english: this name is separate and that name is separate!
phrases.notes: So the spices should not join together, yet the ברייתא says they do.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ דְּבָתַר טַעְמָא אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two opinions were stated (taste vs. name), אביי brings support for his side.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that mixtures are judged by taste.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about spices of different names combining, as explained by חזקיה (because they all sweeten).

steps.title: רבא answers that the spice ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who learns from a פסוק that all Torah prohibitions combine with each other, whatever their name or taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can tell you: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי מאיר. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה said in the name of רבי מאיר: How do we know that all Torah prohibitions combine with each other? The פסוק says 'Do not eat any abomination.' Anything I made an abomination for you is included in 'do not eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes away אביי's proof by saying the ברייתא follows a special opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, all forbidden foods count as one big prohibition, so they combine even when they have different names. That means the spices join for that reason, not because they share a taste. So the ברייתא does not show that taste decides.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא rejects a proof: the source may follow one specific תנא, so it cannot settle a question for everyone.

phrases.english: And Rava would say to you:
Whose is this? It is Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
From where do we know regarding all prohibitions in the Torah
that they combine with one another?
As it says: "Do not eat any abomination,"
anything that I made an abomination for you
is included in 'do not eat.'
phrases.notes: All forbidden foods count as one prohibition, so they join together even with different names.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר לָךְ: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought by אביי in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the spice ברייתא only; רבא's view about names stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The spices may combine because of רבי מאיר's rule that all prohibitions join, not because they share a taste.

steps.title: Vinegar into wine and wine into vinegar
steps.stepSummary: If forbidden vinegar falls into wine, everyone agrees it forbids only by נותן טעם. If forbidden wine falls into vinegar, אביי says any amount forbids and רבא says only נותן טעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Vinegar into wine: everyone agrees it forbids only if it gives taste. Wine into vinegar: אביי says even a tiny amount forbids, and רבא says only if it gives taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case about forbidden wine and vinegar mixing, with an agreed half and a disputed half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The direction of the mixing matters. When vinegar falls into wine, all agree on נותן טעם. When wine falls into vinegar, אביי is stricter and forbids any amount, while רבא still needs taste.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch which liquid is falling into which. The same two liquids get different rulings depending on direction.

phrases.english: Vinegar into wine:
phrases.notes: He means forbidden vinegar falling into permitted wine.

phrases.english: everyone agrees it is by giving taste.
Wine into vinegar:
Abaye said: by any amount,
and Rava said: by giving taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַלָּא לְגוֹ חַמְרָא דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the spice proof to a new mixing case between אביי and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vinegar into wine forbids by נותן טעם according to all; wine into vinegar is disputed: אביי says any amount, רבא says נותן טעם.

steps.title: Restating אביי's view to explain it
